label: First flight

what_happens.title: What happens on a plane trip
goals: The trip has steps: airport, bags, security gate, waiting, boarding, flying, landing
Each step is short and the family stays together
At the end the plane lands and the trip goes on
what_happens.parentSkill: Say the trip steps in order using a toy plane, and let your child fly it.

who_is_there.title: Who helps on a plane trip
goals: Security helpers check bags and shoes to keep everyone safe
Flight attendants help passengers; pilots fly the plane and train for a long time
Lots of other families and kids fly too
who_is_there.parentSkill: Point out the helpers by their jobs: 'That person checks bags so everyone is safe.'

what_i_do.title: What I do on the plane
goals: Walk through the gate, put shoes and toys in a tray
Buckle the seatbelt, look out of the window, have a snack
Chew, sip or yawn when the ears feel full
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise buckling a belt and 'chew and sip' for the ears at home.

if_scared.title: If I feel scared on the plane
goals: Engines are loud and a plane can feel bumpy; that is normal
Ears may feel full or pop, and swallowing helps
Planes are flown by trained pilots, and the seatbelt holds you snug
if_scared.parentSkill: Stay calm and name what is happening: 'That's a bump. The seatbelt is holding us.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise flying
goals: Play airport at home with a tray, a pretend gate and chairs as seats
Practise buckling up and chewing for the ears
Go through the trip once more, ending with landing
rehearsal.parentSkill: Let your child be the pilot announcing each step.

steps: Arrive at the airport and give the big bags to a helper
Walk through the security gate and put shoes and toys in a tray
Wait at the gate and watch the planes
Walk onto the plane and find the seats
Buckle the seatbelt and take off
Snack, look out of the window, rest
Land, unbuckle and walk off the plane
sensory: the loud hum of the engines
a push back into the seat at take-off
ears that feel full or pop
small bumps like a car on a bumpy road
clouds and tiny houses out of the window
a tiny toilet with a loud whoosh flush
honestyNotes: Ears may hurt a little or pop; swallowing helps. Bumps can happen and feel strange. Never promise 'nothing can go wrong'; say pilots train for a long time and planes are built to fly through bumps.

fallbackAnswer: Your ears may feel full, or they may pop, and sometimes that feels a little sore.
Chewing, sipping water or a big yawn helps the feeling go away.
Pilots learn for a long time to fly planes safely.
Sometimes the plane feels bumpy, like a car on a bumpy road, and the seatbelt holds you snug.
At the security gate, helpers check shoes and bags to keep everyone safe.
You put your shoes in a tray, walk through, and put them right back on.

questionButtons.text: Why is the plane so loud?
fallbackAnswer: The engines hum loudly so the plane can go fast and fly.
Headphones or soft hands over your ears can make the sound smaller.
You can hold hands when the plane takes off.

questionButtons.text: What will I do on the plane?
fallbackAnswer: You can look out of the window, have a snack and play with your toys.
Some people even take a nap.

questionButtons.text: Is there a toilet on the plane?
fallbackAnswer: Yes. There is a tiny toilet with a very loud whoosh when it flushes.
You can go with [[GROWNUP]], and you can cover your ears for the whoosh.
Big suitcases ride in the tummy of the plane.
Your small bag stays with you, and the suitcase waits for you at the end.

questionButtons.text: Can I sleep on the plane?
fallbackAnswer: Yes. You can lean on [[GROWNUP]] or on a little pillow.
The seatbelt stays on while you sleep, like a gentle hug.

techniques.label: Chewing and sipping for the ears
techniques.how: At take-off and landing offer a drink, a snack to chew, or a pacifier, and practise big yawns.

techniques.label: Headphones or earmuffs
techniques.how: Bring headphones or soft earmuffs to make the engine sound smaller.

techniques.label: Holding hands
techniques.how: Hold your child's hand at take-off, at landing and through bumps.

techniques.label: The seatbelt hug
techniques.how: Call the seatbelt 'a hug from the plane' and practise buckling it at home.

techniques.label: Window spotting game
techniques.how: Play 'I spy' out of the window: clouds, roads, tiny cars.

techniques.label: Security gate preview
techniques.how: Explain the tray and the gate beforehand; a helper may check bags or ask to look, and you stay right next to your child.

techniques.label: A busy bag
techniques.how: Pack a few small toys, a book and stickers so waiting has something to do; other kids on board may wave too.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Holding my own ticket
techniques.how: Let your child hold a boarding pass (or a drawn one) and show it at the gate.

techniques.label: Following the flight on a map
techniques.how: Show the start and the end of the trip on a map and point to where the plane is now.

ritual: Land and see who is waiting

pain: Your ears might feel full. Let's chew and sip together.
A big yawn can help your ears pop.
safety: Pilots practise for a long time to fly safely.
Bumps feel funny, and the seatbelt holds us snug.
unknown: First the gate, then the waiting room, then the plane.
Shoes go in the tray and come right back.
sensory: The engines are loud. Headphones make it smaller.
That push in your seat means we're taking off.
separation: We sit together the whole flight.
I'll walk through the gate right after you.
strangers: The helpers at the airport check bags to keep everyone safe.
Flight attendants help everyone on the plane.
body: A helper might look at your bag or your shoes. I stay right next to you.
You can always tell me if something feels wrong.
social: Lots of families fly. Maybe a kid will wave at you.
We can play a quiet game so everyone can rest.
love: I'm right here with you, all the way.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] will fly on a plane.
First, [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] go to a big airport.
A helper takes the big bags, and they get a ride on a moving belt.
Next comes the security gate, where shoes and toys go in a tray.
Then everyone waits by the big windows and watches the planes.
Then [[CHILD]] walks onto the plane and finds a seat.
Click goes the seatbelt, snug like a hug.
The engines hum, the plane rolls fast, and up it goes into the sky.
After a snack and a look at the clouds, the plane comes down and lands.
At the security gate there are helpers in uniforms.
Their job is to check bags and shoes so everyone is safe.
They might say, shoes in the tray, please.
[[CHILD]] puts the shoes in, walks through the gate, and puts them right back on.
[[GROWNUP]] walks through right after.
On the plane, flight attendants say hello and help everyone find a seat.
In front, the pilots fly the plane.
Pilots learn for a long, long time to fly safely.
There are lots of other people and families on the plane too.
Maybe a kid will wave at [[CHILD]] from across the aisle.
On the plane, [[CHILD]] has some jobs.
Sit in the seat next to [[GROWNUP]] and click the seatbelt.
When the plane goes up, [[CHILD]] can hold [[GROWNUP]]'s hand.
Then there is time to look out of the window, have a snack and play with a toy.
When the plane goes up and comes down, ears can feel full.
Sometimes they pop with a funny little sound.
[[CHILD]] can chew a snack, take a sip of water, or do a big lion yawn.
That helps the ears feel better.
[[CHILD]] knows the ear trick now.
A plane can be loud, like a big humming fan.
Sometimes the plane feels bumpy, like a car on a bumpy road.
The seatbelt holds [[CHILD]] snug, and the pilots know what to do with bumps.
[[CHILD]] can put on headphones and hold [[GROWNUP]]'s hand.
If [[CHILD]]'s ears feel sore, there is the ear trick: chew, sip, or yawn.
[[GROWNUP]] sits right next to [[CHILD]] the whole time.
When something feels strange, [[CHILD]] can smell a flower and blow out a candle, slow and soft.
Being brave means trying, even when it feels new.
Tonight [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] play airport at home.
Two chairs are the plane seats, and a box is the security tray.
Shoes go in the tray, then [[CHILD]] walks through the pretend gate.
Next, [[CHILD]] sits down and clicks a pretend seatbelt.
Now try the ear trick: a big lion yawn!
Let's say the trip once more.
First the airport and the bags, then the security gate and the tray.
Next, the plane, the seatbelt and up into the sky.
After that, snacks, clouds and landing.
[[GROWNUP]] is proud of [[CHILD]] for practising every step.

[[GROWNUP]] stays next to me.
